text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, even for someone who did not write it. One key idea is using clear names for variables and functions, so their purpose is obvious. Following common naming conventions also helps other developers read your work quickly. Another important point is keeping functions small and focused on one task. When functions do too many things, they become hard to test and reuse. Clean code is also easier to maintain, because fixing bugs or adding new features takes less time and causes fewer mistakes.
